why: Inserting a rule to avoid cutting between verbs and their essential complements made the model less likely to split verb–object/resultative chunks, giving small average gains (largest in the shortest latency bin ≤3) but also shifting many cuts so that punctuation or quotation marks became isolated fragments — those shifted cuts produced the large negative tail movements and left the net effect marginal.
lesson: Respect verb–complement binding but avoid moving cuts in a way that leaves punctuation/quotes or other tiny tokens as isolated pieces; ensure punctuation stays attached to the unit it punctuates when enforcing verb-complement constraints.
